title: Endpoint Service Contract Spec: quantile UX SLI, error-budget banking & graceful region evacuation
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: produce a concrete, operational SLO/SLI and error-budget banking policy for user-facing endpoints that explicitly ties user-experience quantiles to automatic region evacuation and tenant-aware circuit breakers. This ticket captures the spec, decision log, rollout steps, and the required dashboards/runbooks.

Scope: per-endpoint (route+model) SLI definitions that measure both quality (semantic correctness proxy via classifier+eval set) and latency tail (p50/p95/p99). Define an error-budget banking model allowing short-term borrowing across low-traffic model variants, and a staged failover plan that triggers regional evacuation and soft-load-shedding before hard circuit breaker tripping. Excluded: billing or rate-limit quota changes, model retraining guidance.
updates: 2026-02-16 - Marisol Vega: Kickoff notes added; linked baseline SLO taxonomy and prior SLI experiments. Decision to use quantile-based UX SLI (p90 of a similarity score) rather than only token-level metrics.

2026-02-22 - Liam O'Connor: Added initial draft thresholds: latency p99 < 1.2s for interactive routes, p95 < 500ms for embeddings. Proposed UX SLI: 95% of requests must have semantic-similarity >= 0.78 on curated prompt set over 24h window.
2026-02-28 - Design review (Aisha Patel): Requested retention of label-level breakdowns in dashboards for rapid triage. Added label to ensure per-tenant SLI bucketing.

2026-03-03 - Engineering review (Ravi Menon): Raised trade-off: similarity classifier introduces 0.5% additional false-positive drift; proposed mitigation by combining sample-based human checks and a decay factor in banking model.
2026-03-05 - PM review (Daniel Ko): Approved rollout gating criteria and suggested adding canary with synthetic traffic in eu-west-1 before global activation.

2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Incorporated feedback, authored runbook steps and circuit-breaker thresholds. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387. Dashboards: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/redwood/endpoint-sli-summary. Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RINF/pages/178392903/Endpoint+Service+Contract+Spec
acceptance_criteria: Final spec doc published in Confluence with decision log and glossary
Datadog dashboards created for per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 latency and UX similarity quantiles
Automated alerting configured: error-budget burn rate > 3x for 1h triggers canary failover to next region
Circuit breaker policy implemented in router: soft-threshold (queue length based) and hard-threshold (error-rate-based) with tenant-aware weights
Runbook with step-by-step evacuation and un-evacuation commands exists and is verified in canary (eu-west-1 synthetic run)
notes: Design decision: use a composite SLI composed of semantic-similarity quantile + latency tail instead of a single availability number to better reflect user experience for generative endpoints.

Banking policy: endpoints with low sustained traffic can lend up to 20% of their monthly error-budget to sibling model variants under the same product route; borrowing capped at 2 days and requires automated rollback if borrow triggers for >24h continuously.

Failover sequencing: 1) prefix KV cache rewind and local fallback (0-30s), 2) route-level soft load-shedding (degrade to lower-cost quantized variant) (30-120s), 3) region evacuation (shift new traffic) (2-10m), 4) hard circuit-breaker (reject) if error budget exhausted despite evacuation.

Tenant-aware circuit breakers: tenants consuming >5% of route QPS get protected slices; however, in extreme overload tenants can be back-pressured based on SLA tier. Implementation to be compatible with existing quota and billing layers.
Telemetry notes: include sample-set of requests (1/1000) for offline similarity re-eval to detect classifier drift; tag samples with model_version, route, region, tenant_id for attribution.

Rollout plan: feature flag gated, execute canary in eu-west-1 using synthetic traffic generator (see canary playbook), then expand to NA regions in waves over two days with monitoring runbooks on standby.
